objective: Make the hosted-CI ship gate logically sound: distinguish execution inside CI from completed-green CI, while preserving a green workflow and fail-closed final release.
starting_state: v0.14-rc2; 60 tests; local 9/10 gates; hosted CI absent; release verifier treated an in-job attestation as hosted_ci_green.
sources_datasets_consulted: No new empirical dataset; this run targeted release correctness and reproducibility semantics.
failures_rejected_approaches: Rejected the rc2 semantics that an attestation generated while a workflow is running can prove that workflow completed green.

Initial two-phase implementation made the CI workflow impossible to pass because the completed-run record cannot exist until after the job finishes; corrected by adding explicit CI mode versus final release mode.
assumptions: GitHub Actions is the intended hosted CI provider.
A final ship decision must be based on GitHub's completed run state, not self-attestation from within the still-running job.
architectural_decisions: Two-phase CI evidence: in-job hosted execution attestation plus post-run completed-success evidence bound to the commit.
CI mode may pass without post-run evidence; final mode may not.
ci_state: Local suite/eval green. Hosted CI remains externally blocked because no Radiant repository is accessible. Final verifier intentionally fails locally on hosted_ci_execution and hosted_ci_completed_green.
weakest_link: External repository/hosted-CI publication and observation; no remaining local release-engineering blocker identified.
exact_next_action: Push this exact rc3 candidate to the intended Radiant GitHub repository. Let Actions run in --ci mode. After GitHub reports completed/success, capture a commit-bound completed_ci_run.json from the GitHub run, rerun final release verification, and ship v1.0 only if 11/11 final gates pass.
